content: The ERASURE trial, officially titled Regression of Coronary Atherosclerotic Lesions After rHDL Infusions in Acute Coronary Syndrome Patients as Assessed by Intravascular Ultrasound, aimed to evaluate the effects of reconstituted HDL (rHDL) on atheromatous plaque volume using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS). The study was registered on 09/19/2013 under the identification number NCT00225719. Eligibility Criteria Inclusion Criteria: Participants were required to be male or female, aged between 30 and 75 years. They must have experienced a recent acute coronary syndrome (ACS) event within the last 14 days. ACS was defined as unstable angina, non-Q wave myocardial infarction, or ST elevation indicative of myocardial infarction. Exclusion Criteria: Patients with greater than 50% stenosis in the left main coronary artery were excluded. Those with renal insufficiency, liver or hepatic disease, or uncontrolled diabetes mellitus were not eligible. Individuals with symptomatic heart failure classified as NYHA class III or IV were excluded. Patients with a known soybean allergy (a component of the CSL-111 infusion) were not eligible. A history of alcohol or drug abuse disqualified participants. Patients on warfarin or heparin anticoagulation therapy during the infusion period were excluded. Outcomes Primary Outcomes: The primary outcome was the percentage difference in atheroma volume between the follow-up and baseline measurements as assessed by IVUS. Secondary Outcomes: Secondary outcomes included the absolute change in coronary score, defined as the mean minimal lumen diameter for all measured lesions on angiography. Changes in plaque volume and characterization on IVUS were also assessed. Safety and Observations The safety profile of CSL-111 was thoroughly evaluated. Elevations in liver function tests, particularly within 24 hours of infusion, were observed but were subclinical and resolved without intervention. A transient increase in unconjugated bilirubin was also noted, which was self-limiting. Conclusion Short-term infusions of CSL-111 demonstrated significant improvements in plaque characterization index and coronary score on angiography. However, there were no significant changes in plaque or atheroma volume. The clinical relevance of these findings remains unclear and requires further investigation.
